# 2 Samuel Chapter 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 194v–195r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_022_page_001.jpg, 2SA_022_page_002.jpg, 2SA_022_page_003.jpg, 2SA_022_page_004.jpg

---

**1** David sang this song to the LORD on the day the LORD rescued him from all his enemies and from Saul.

**2** He sang:
"The LORD is my rock, my fortress, my rescuer —

**3** my God is the bedrock where I find shelter;
my shield, the horn that saves me,
my stronghold, my refuge,
my savior — you rescue me from violence.

**4** I call out to the LORD — he deserves all praise —
and I am saved from my enemies.

**5** The waves of death crashed over me,
the flood of destruction swept me away in terror.

**6** The ropes of the grave wrapped around me;
death's traps lay waiting in my path.

**7** In my anguish I cried out to the LORD;
I called to my God for help.
From his temple he heard my voice —
my cry for help reached his ears.

**8** Then the earth lurched and shook;
the foundations of the sky trembled
and reeled, because he burned with anger.

**9** Smoke poured from his nostrils,
devouring fire blazed from his mouth;
white-hot coals shot out from him.

**10** He tore open the heavens and came down,
with storm-clouds black beneath his feet.

**11** He mounted a winged creature and flew;
he appeared, riding the wings of the wind.

**12** He wrapped himself in darkness like a tent,
in masses of water and thick banks of cloud.

**13** Out of the brightness before him
coals of fire blazed.

**14** The LORD thundered from heaven;
the voice of the Most High rang out.

**15** He shot his arrows and scattered my enemies;
he hurled lightning and threw them into panic.

**16** Then the ocean floor was exposed,
the foundations of the world laid bare,
at the LORD's roar of rebuke,
at the blast of breath from his nostrils.

**17** He reached down from on high and seized me;
he pulled me out of the deep waters.

**18** He rescued me from my powerful enemy,
from those who hated me — they were too strong for me.

**19** They ambushed me on the worst day of my life,
but the LORD was there to hold me up.

**20** He brought me out into the open;
he rescued me because he wanted me.

**21** The LORD dealt with me as my righteousness deserved;
he repaid me because my hands were clean.

**22** For I have followed the LORD's ways
and have not turned from my God to do evil.

**23** All his laws were before me;
I never pushed aside his commands.

**24** I was wholly his,
and I kept myself from giving in to my sin.

**25** So the LORD repaid me for my righteousness,
for my cleanness in his sight.

**26** To the faithful you prove faithful;
to the blameless warrior you prove blameless.

**27** To the pure you prove pure,
but to the twisted you prove shrewd.

**28** You save those who are humble,
but your eyes are on the proud — to bring them down.

**29** You, LORD, are my lamp;
the LORD turns my darkness into light.

**30** With you I can charge an army;
with my God I can scale any wall.

**31** God's way is flawless.
The LORD's word has been tested in the fire.
He is a shield for everyone who runs to him for safety.

**32** For who is God except the LORD?
Who is solid rock except our God?

**33** God is my mighty fortress;
he clears the way for the blameless.

**34** He makes my feet as sure as a deer's
and sets me on the heights.

**35** He trains my hands for combat
so my arms can bend a bow of bronze.

**36** You gave me the shield of your salvation,
and your willingness to answer made me great.

**37** You cleared a wide path for my feet,
and my ankles never gave way.

**38** I chased my enemies and wiped them out;
I did not stop until they were finished.

**39** I struck them down and crushed them — they could not get up;
they fell at my feet.

**40** You armed me with strength for the fight;
you forced my opponents to their knees before me.

**41** You made my enemies turn and run,
and I destroyed everyone who hated me.

**42** They screamed for help, but no one came to save them;
they cried out to the LORD, but he was silent.

**43** I ground them to powder, fine as dust;
I trampled them like mud in the streets.

**44** You rescued me from my people's conflicts;
you placed me at the head of nations.
People I never knew now serve me.

**45** Foreigners come crawling;
the moment they hear of me, they submit.

**46** Foreigners lose their nerve
and come shaking out of their hiding places.

**47** The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock!
Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation!

**48** He is the God who avenges me,
who brings nations under my feet,

**49** who frees me from my enemies.
You lift me above my attackers;
you snatch me from violent men.

**50** For this I will praise you, LORD, among the nations;
I will sing to your name.

**51** He is a tower of victory for his king.
He shows unfailing covenant-faithfulness to his anointed,
to David and his descendants forever."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verses 2-3 — The avalanche of metaphors:** David doesn't choose one image for God — he heaps up seven in two verses: rock, fortress, deliverer, bedrock, shield, horn, stronghold. This is a man who has hidden in caves, run through deserts, scaled cliffs, and survived ambushes. Every metaphor comes from lived experience. The theology is not abstract — it is rock and bronze and walls.

**Verse 5 — "waves of death":** The Hebrew *mishberey mavet* evokes the sea as a force of chaos and annihilation. In the ancient Near Eastern worldview, the deep waters (*tehom*) represent primordial chaos that only God can master. David's enemies are not merely human — they are cosmic in their threat.

**Verses 8-16 — The theophany:** This is one of the most powerful descriptions of God's appearance in all of Scripture. The earth shakes, smoke and fire pour from God's face, the heavens split open, God rides the storm — all to rescue one man. The theological audacity is staggering: the God who controls earthquakes, volcanoes, and thunderstorms deploys the entire arsenal of creation because David called out for help.

**Verse 11 — "appeared" vs. Psalm 18's "soared":** The 2 Samuel text says God *appeared* on the wings of the wind — he became visible, manifested. Psalm 18 says he *soared*. Both are extraordinary, but the 2 Samuel version emphasizes revelation: in the storm, you can see God.

**Verse 26-27 — The mirror principle:** God becomes a reflection of the person who approaches him. To the loyal, God is loyal. To the pure, God is pure. To the twisted, God becomes — terrifyingly — twisted. This is not moral relativism; it is moral reciprocity. You get the God you bring.

**Verse 31 — "tested in the fire":** The Hebrew *tserufah* is metallurgical language — refined, smelted, purified. God's word has been through the furnace. What remains is pure.

**Verse 51 — "forever":** The poem ends with *'ad-olam* — into eternity. David's song moves from personal rescue (vv.2-20) to moral reflection (vv.21-28) to military triumph (vv.29-46) and finally to eternal promise (vv.47-51). The covenant with David and his seed is the destination the entire poem has been building toward.

*— PNEUMA*
